paragraphs: Five teenage boys died in County Kildare, Ireland, after driving a stolen BMW the wrong way down a highway and colliding head-on with another car.

The victims in the second vehicle, a family traveling to the airport, suffered severe injuries, and two adults remain in critical condition. Accounts belonging to some of the deceased boys contained videos showing stolen cars, reckless driving, and escaping police pursuits. Following the horrific incident, Ireland’s media regulator contacted TikTok to investigate its efforts in removing dangerous joyriding content.

Irish Prime Minister condemned the behavior and stated that reckless driving is increasingly staged to gain popularity and likes on social media platforms. Police representatives warned that rival youth gangs actively try to outdo each other online through dangerous driving stunts. In response, TikTok stated that it is closely monitoring related content and continuously removing accounts that violate safety rules regarding criminal behavior.

paragraphs: Five teenagers died in Ireland after driving a stolen car the wrong way on a busy highway.
Their car crashed directly into another vehicle carrying a family to the airport. Four family members were seriously injured, and two women are still fighting for their lives in the hospital.

Reports revealed that the boys had previously posted videos on social media which showed stolen cars and dangerous driving to get likes and followers on social media. The Irish government and police blamed social media platforms for encouraging this reckless behavior.

Officials are now contacting TikTok to ensure the company takes down these dangerous videos. TikTok claimed it is actively monitoring the platform and deleting accounts that break its rules against illegal actions.

paragraphs: Five young boys die in a car crash in Ireland. They steal a car. Then, they drive on the wrong side of a highway. They hit another car with a family inside. Four people in the family are in the hospital with bad injuries.
Police say that the teenagers drive fast and dangerously to make short videos for social media. They wanted to get likes and new friends online. Many young boys do it now.
The Irish government wants TikTok to stop these dangerous videos. TikTok says that it deletes bad videos and accounts which break safety rules.
